verificationEvidence.claim: WHAT: submit() awaits onSave(draft) with no error handling and is invoked as `void submit()`, so a rejected onSave produces an unhandled promise rejection and the errors state is never updated. WHY: when the save/create request fails, the user sees no error message and the button appears to do nothing (silent failure), and the rejected promise is unhandled. HOW: wrap the call in try/catch and surface the failure via setErrors, e.g. `if (problems.length === 0) { try { await onSave(draft); } catch { setErrors(['Could not save the customer']); } }`.
verificationEvidence.rationale: Confirmed: submit() (lines 19-23) awaits onSave(draft) with no error handling and is called as `void submit()` (line 33). onSave is typed Promise<void> and can reject (e.g. failed save/create request), yielding an unhandled promise rejection while errors state is never updated — silent failure to the user. The failure path is real and reachable. This is a distinct issue from the previous decision (BillingSection visibility in create mode), so it is not a repeat.
